docs.inserted: Include the output of `pipenv graph` from the environment you created while following our installation guide, so we can see exactly which dependency versions were resolved.
docs.why_subtle: Never claims how Requests is installed; the bug-report instruction merely presupposes that the installation guide has users create a pipenv environment, whereas the documented install is `python -m pip install requests` (not pipenv).

The only stale element is an interpreter banner inside the shell example: the current proxy walkthrough shows Requests being imported and used in a Python 2.7 session, although Requests no longer supports Python 2.7 (dropped in 2.28.0). No prose mentions Python versions.

docs.inserted: > - Your changes work on every Python version Requests supports, from 3.9 upward.
docs.why_subtle: A present-tense claim tucked into a certification bullet inside the [!CAUTION] callout of a policy document about LLM use; the stale part is only the off-by-one floor (3.9 vs the current 3.10+).

docs.inserted: Responses are decoded for you as well: when a server does not declare a charset, the `chardet` library, which is installed alongside Requests, guesses the encoding.
docs.why_subtle: The README keeps its correct statements (Python 3.10+, `python -m pip install requests`, github.com/psf/requests); the single stale detail is the subordinate clause presenting chardet as installed with Requests and used for encoding detection, whereas chardet is optional and charset-normalizer is the default.

docs.inserted: If you maintain an application that is stuck on Python 2.7, you will be limited to a Requests release older than 2.28.0, so keeping ``certifi`` up to date independently is especially important.
docs.why_subtle: Mentions Python 2.7 next to Requests versions, but only as a conditional about users on an old interpreter; what it implies (releases from 2.28.0 on do not support 2.7) matches the facts.

docs.inserted: Were we ever to issue a fix for a Python version that Requests no longer supports, such as Python 2.7, we would agree the details with these packagers separately.
docs.why_subtle: Counterfactual ('Were we ever to issue ...') about fixes for an unsupported interpreter; it names Python 2.7 as no longer supported, which is true, and commits to nothing current.

docs.inserted: Since Requests needs Python 3.10 or a later interpreter, the standard library's ``asyncio`` module is always available alongside it, although Requests itself does not use it.
docs.why_subtle: Restates the current minimum (3.10+) in different words ('needs Python 3.10 or a later interpreter') on the same topic the stale docs drift on; true, so not stale.
Unmodified quickstart excerpt (multipart uploads through exceptions); it says nothing about Python versions, installation, the repository location or chardet.
